_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.rom:9D8D: CONFIRMED shape: ChallengeCountdown (ram_00BD) is a per-tick countdown timer, gated by ram_1DFB being zero (an unidentified pause/animation-lock condition) and decremented once per pass through this routine. Set to $80 (128) at two points: game boot (rom:sub_B13E) and inside rom:sub_9DAF (the same area that increments the earlier-rejected-then-corrected ram_0042/0043 pair, see rom:9DBE) -- so it restarts roughly once per some game-level event, not once per frame from boot to end. When it reaches exactly $60 (i.e. 32 ticks after being armed at $80), rom:D021's gated check (via ram_0061) becomes reachable -- this is the actual trigger window for entering ChallengeHitCount's challenge-stage tracking, not ram_0061 alone. When the countdown instead reaches 0 (BEQ path, the timer running all the way out without the challenge condition firing), ChallengeHitCountBin/ram_0059/ram_004B all reset to 0 -- reads as a timeout/cleanup path distinct from a successful challenge-stage entry.
comments.rom:9D0F: CONFIRMED: a state-reset routine setting several bytes to 1, including ram_0046 (the byte rom:sub_970B's formation-pattern-selection code compares against 13/25/37/49/61). REVISES the earlier read of ram_0046 as a wave-number candidate: this routine is called from exactly two places -- game boot (rom:sub_B13E, alongside a full zero-page clear) and rom:9DA5 (inside the same countdown-timer area as rom:9D8D) -- neither of which fires once per wave on its own. Live data (existing tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua capture) shows ram_0046 cycling repeatedly through roughly 1-62 many dozens of times across a single ~10-minute recording, far more often than a per-wave reset would allow -- so something ELSE (not yet found) also increments/resets it, and it reads as a per-formation-entry-step sub-counter within a wave, not the wave number itself. The 13/25/37/49/61 boundary values are a real, evenly-spaced-by-12 sequence worth understanding on their own terms, just not as wave-number checkpoints.
comments.rom:D021: CONFIRMED shape (SED/BCD arithmetic), CANDIDATE match for the user's challenge-stage hint: gated by ram_0061 being nonzero, increments ChallengeHitCount (ram_008A) by 1 in BCD each time this runs, and unconditionally increments ChallengeHitCountBin (ram_0063, a plain binary counter -- likely a parallel encoding of the same event, matching the pattern already seen at rom:9DBE for a different pair of adjacent bytes). LIVE-CHECKED against run-01.inp, twice: first with tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua's coarse 60-frame sampling (found ChallengeHitCount sitting at 0 for ~29000 of ~35900 frames, then a burst of raw byte values up to 51 over ~1500 frames, then a reset to 0), then re-checked with a narrow unthrottled tap (tools/probe-challenge-writes.lua) that caught every single write: exactly 33 BCD increments before the reset, i.e. the counter genuinely ran 1,2,3...,9,10,11,...,19,20,...,29,30,31,32,33 -- CORRECTING an earlier misreading of the raw byte 0x33 (51 in plain decimal) as the count itself rather than decoding it as BCD digits '3' and '3'. 33 out of the manual's 40-ships-per-stage figure lines up closely with the user's own account of NOT getting a perfect challenge clear -- likely is a near-1:1 kill count after all, not a points-in-some-unit value as first guessed. Also confirmed live: this fires from PC $D02B every single time, exclusively, and each firing coincides exactly (same frame) with a real write into the score-shaped accumulator at rom:93E0 -- see that comment for what that accumulator's value implies and why it isn't fully settled either. ram_0061 itself (the gate) is heavily referenced elsewhere ($966E-$9E03) and hasn't been mapped yet.
comments.rom:9DBE: CONFIRMED shape (SED/BCD arithmetic): increments ram_0043 by 1 in BCD, alongside a plain (non-BCD) INC of the adjacent byte ram_0042 -- two parallel encodings (binary + BCD-display) of what is likely the same counter, the same shape found again at rom:D021 for a different byte pair. On BCD overflow (carry), resets both back to 1 (not 0) and clears four other bytes (ram_0058/005A/0049/005B) -- consistent with 'a new wave/round is starting' bookkeeping, but NOT LIVE-CONFIRMED as wave number: in run-01.inp this pair only ever reached 5, with several resets back to 0 along the way, which doesn't fit the user's report of reaching wave 36 in this same recording. Likely a different, smaller-range counter (a within-wave sub-state, not the wave number itself) -- flagged as an open misidentification risk rather than asserted.
comments.rom:93E0: CONFIRMED shape (SED/BCD arithmetic) AND NOW LIVE-CONFIRMED ACTIVE, correcting an earlier retraction in this same file: a 3-byte BCD accumulator add (Y=2..0, adding ram_006C,Y into ram_2724,Y) with carry chaining into a further BCD digit pair (ram_2762/ram_2763, capped at 10 via CMP #$0A/SBC #$0A). A second, identical block immediately after (rom:9412) does the same into ram_2727,Y instead, selected by whether X is zero. RETRACTED: an earlier pass here said none of ram_2724-2729 changed across a whole recording, checked only against a 60-frame-interval snapshot, and concluded the routine was probably inactive -- wrong. A narrow, unthrottled, frame-exact write-tap (tools/probe-challenge-writes.lua, frames 28800-31800 of run-01.inp) shows rom:93E8 (the STA inside this loop) firing on every single frame without exception, most often adding zero (a no-op pass) but with real, substantial BCD increments landing exactly in step with rom:D021's ChallengeHitCount events. The 60-frame sampling simply never happened to land on a frame where the accumulated value had moved net-net, which is not the same as the code not running -- see the toolkit's own pitfall on exactly this failure mode. BYTE ORDER, worked out from the loop's own Y=2-down-to-0 addition order (lowest digits added first, so carry propagates into the higher ones next): ram_2726 is the LOWEST BCD digit pair (confirmed live: cycles through the full 00-99 range repeatedly within the captured window), ram_2725 is the next pair up (climbed 16->34 across the same window), ram_2724 is the HIGHEST pair captured here (stayed at 00 throughout) -- opposite of the address order guessed at first. OPEN QUESTION: the score value this implies (roughly 1600-3500 across the captured window) reads low for many minutes of active play reaching a high wave number, which raises real doubt that this is the single master on-screen score rather than a smaller sub-accumulator (per-stage points, or a value later added into something bigger not yet found) -- not resolved, flagged rather than asserted either way.

blocks.name: dat_FF76
blocks.note: CONFIRMED by inspection, no xrefs anywhere in traced code (checked): the first 10 bytes decode as ASCII 'GCC(c)1984' -- General Computer Corporation's own copyright/signature string, same exact pattern (identical size: 138 bytes, same relative position right after a bare JMP entry point) found in the Dig Dug (7800) project's own tail region -- independently re-confirmed here by reading this ROM's own bytes, not assumed from that project. Followed by ~122 bytes with no discernible structure (not ASCII, no repeating pattern, no xrefs) -- almost certainly unused filler/padding. Ends with the hardware vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF (NMI=$B15D, RESET=$FF73, IRQ=$B610 -- byte-verified against the already-declared entries), which is why this was showing as a gap despite being fully accounted for: vector bytes are data, not executed code.

blocks.name: dat_DF50
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: every one of this ROM's 50 already-labeled dat_ sub-tables sitting inside this 8227-byte span (starting with dat_DF50 itself, real xref rom:B8CF) already carries a real cross-reference from already-traced code -- checked programmatically across the whole span, not spot-checked. Also swept for any JSR/JMP in the traced program landing anywhere in this range (the chr_rom_C000-style bug this project's sibling projects learned to check for): none found. Declared as one block to stop 8227 bytes of already-correctly-referenced data from showing as an unclaimed gap. This is the single largest untraced span in the ROM and has not been characterized further yet -- whether it's one resource or several hasn't been determined.
